concept.title: Navigation and the home page
concept.shortdesc: Every page carries a sidebar tree built from your map; the home page is generated from the map's own metadata.

section.title: The sidebar
section.p: The sidebar lists the whole publication, follows your map's hierarchy, and marks the page being read. With JavaScript available it gains a menu toggle on small screens and expand/collapse controls on branches, with the current page's ancestors open; without JavaScript the full tree simply stays visible, so nothing is ever unreachable.

Topics with toc="no" stay out of the tree but are still built and linkable — useful for large reference sets addressed by cross-reference rather than browsing, as in the Open Referral UK publications.

section.title: The home page
section.p: The site's index.html shows the publication title and a contents tree. Bookmaps contribute more: the alternative book title becomes the abstract paragraph, and the book's author and owning organisation appear beneath it — exactly as on this manual's own home page.
section.note: Give each top-level topic a good shortdesc: the accepted landing-page design (decision D-13) will reuse it as the entry's description on richer home-page layouts.
